decisions.question: Item S124a: G15 and G24 say a redaction never contains the payload's own rendering, which cannot hold for a short rendering (RedactedPayload.of('String') renders <redacted String #...>; RedactedPayload.of('a') contains 'a'). What should the guarantees say instead?

options.label: state that a redaction shows only the type name and hash
options.consequence: G24 says the rendering shows nothing of p but its runtime type and hash code, and that p's rendering occurs in it only where it matches part of that text; G15 says the envelope shows the redaction where the payload's rendering would stand and renders the payload no other way; already implied by the format clause the existing case checks exactly, so no new case

options.label: add a guarantee that the payload's toString() is never called
options.consequence: a stronger, new rule that needs a case with a throwing toString(); more than the item asks and more than the format clause already fixes

options.label: keep 'never contains'
options.consequence: a guarantee the shipped package, and any implementation of the Interface, fails for short renderings

decisions.chosen: state that a redaction shows only the type name and hash
decisions.why: The rendering <redacted {typeName} #{hash}> is fully determined by the runtime type and hash code, so 'shows nothing of p but those' is what the format clause already guarantees and what the code does (redacted_payload.dart builds it from runtimeType and hashCode only; envelope.dart's toString never renders a sensitive payload). The substring claim was an overstatement, not a rule.

decisions.question: Item S124b: G15 applied to an envelope that redacted() returned (still sensitive, payload a RedactedPayload) redacts again, so its toString() shows <redacted RedactedPayload #...> and the payload type is lost; the surface fixture's AuditObserver logs exactly this. Which rule does the contract state?

options.label: state the code's choice: redaction applies to any payload
options.consequence: G15 and the Redaction section say redacting a redacted envelope wraps the redaction, and tell a sink to render the envelope itself (whose toString already redacts) or the copy's payload to keep the type name; matches what G15's literal text and the shipped code already do; a later switch to idempotent redaction changes G15 and the code

options.label: idempotent redaction (owner's choice, code change)
options.consequence: redacted() and toString() would keep a payload that is already a RedactedPayload, so the type name survives a second redaction; needs a change to envelope.dart in nidana.model and a G15 amendment, outside this sweep's rule

options.label: leave the text silent
options.consequence: consumers such as the runtime's telemetry observer would repeat the AuditObserver pattern without knowing it loses the type name

decisions.chosen: state the code's choice: redaction applies to any payload
decisions.why: The shipped choice is sound as a rule: one uniform function of the payload, the copy keeps sensitive true so the admission rule (G23) stays honest for it, and nothing is lost when a sink renders the original envelope. G15 as written already says 'replaces a sensitive payload with RedactedPayload.of(payload)' with no exception, so stating the consequence changes no rule. Asked-worthy because the owner may prefer idempotent redaction for diagnostics; that is cheap now, since no consumer phase has shipped, and would fail the new G15 case loudly. Signal that would have changed my mind: a Spec 9.2 sentence requiring the payload type to survive any number of redactions (the Spec is not checked out here).

decisions.question: Item S125a: G24 says a redaction is 'equal for equal payloads', but the Interface's == compares typeName and hash, so RedactedPayload.of(1) and RedactedPayload.of(1.0) differ although 1 == 1.0 and their hash codes agree. Which side gives?

options.label: narrow G24 to payloads of one runtime type
options.consequence: G24 and the Redaction paragraph say equal payloads of one runtime type redact alike and of two runtime types do not, as the Interface's == comment already decided; no code change

decisions.chosen: narrow G24 to payloads of one runtime type
decisions.why: The Interface states == as 'typeName and hash' and typeName as payload.runtimeType.toString(); G24's phrase overstated what those two lines allow, and no implementation of the Interface could meet it. decisions.question: Item S125b: G13 read literally makes an envelope whose payload is NaN unequal to itself, so a Set of envelopes cannot find or remove it. An identical short-circuit is the contract owner's call; what does the code do, and what does the text say?

options.label: state the code's choice: field ==, no identity shortcut
options.consequence: G13 and a new Equality of envelopes paragraph say each field compares with its own == and no identity shortcut, so a NaN-payload envelope is not equal to itself and a Set or Map does not find it, as a Set<double> does not find double.nan; the redacted copy of a sensitive one is equal to itself

options.label: identity shortcut (owner's choice, code change)
options.consequence: identical(this, other) || in envelope.dart's == makes every envelope equal to itself and findable in a Set; contradicts G13's 'exactly when all eight fields are equal', so it needs a G13 amendment and a nidana.model code change, outside this sweep's rule

options.label: leave the text as it is
options.consequence: the rule stays implied by the literal text only, and recorder or test authors learn it from a failing lookup

decisions.chosen: state the code's choice: field ==, no identity shortcut
decisions.why: The shipped == has no shortcut, and G13's literal text already says exactly that; the choice is consistent with how Dart's own collections treat double.nan (List.contains, Set.contains and Map lookup all miss it). Asked-worthy because the probe shows Dart VM records compare fields by identity first (a record holding double.nan, or any value never equal to itself, is equal to itself), so an owner who wants envelopes to behave like records would choose the shortcut; that is cheap before any consumer phase ships and would fail the new G13 case loudly.

decisions.question: The G13, G15 and G24 clauses now state rules (no identity shortcut; redaction of a RedactedPayload; equality by type name and hash) that a seeded implementation could break while passing all 41 cases. Pin them with new behavior cases, or leave them text-only?

options.consequence: the restated rules stay unexecuted, and a deviation in the runtime's own value handling or a future refactor of the package goes unnoticed

decisions.why: A stable contract's rules are meant to be machine-checked, and the brief allows a new case that passes against the shipped package. The G24 case is platform-neutral: it uses a second payload class with the same hash code, and expects the 1 and 1.0 redactions to be equal exactly when their runtime types are, which holds on the VM and is written to hold on the web too (not run there). The first draft of the G13 case compared double.nan with itself, which the analyzer flags (unnecessary_nan_comparison); the case asserts payload.isNaN instead, and the behavior and surface fixtures analyze clean.

decisions.question: Item S133: topic-model@v1 cites ADR-003 items in its Interface and in G12 and G25, but its Governed by omits ADR-003 and ADR-003's affects omits topic-model@v1, so hsdd-config leaves ADR-003 out of a phase that consumes topic-model@v1 alone. Add the link in both places, or leave it?

options.label: leave it, citing ADR-003's amendment of 2026-10-17
options.consequence: Governed by stays [ADR-001, ADR-002]; a phase that consumes only topic-model@v1 gets no ADR-003 context, which it does not need, and impl-gate keeps its warning

options.label: add ADR-003 to Governed by (and to ADR-003's affects through hsdd-adr)
options.consequence: a two-skill change; adding only this side would break ADR-003's rule (its 2026-10-21 amendment) that every header carrying ADR-003 is named in its affects, and ADR-003 is outside this step's write set (S154 touches ADR-001 only)

decisions.chosen: leave it, citing ADR-003's amendment of 2026-10-17
decisions.why: The amendment's test is whether ADR-003 constrains a guarantee consumers rely on; what it asks of topic-model (no clock, timestamps and ids as arguments: G12, G25, item 8) binds only the producer, nidana.model, which affects names. The reason still holds for the other two citations, which the amendment did not name: the item 9 citation behind G5 (no dispatcher hint) predates it (topic-model authored in S06, amendment in S18) and is a declaration shape the producer ships, while the one-zone runtime rule consumers rely on is bus-api@v2's, governed by ADR-003; the item 2 citation only points at bus-api@v2's observer guarantees. The consumers of topic-model@v1 in nidana.runtime, nidana.navigation, nidana.flutter and nidana.integration belong to nodes ADR-003 names, and the tooling consumers (lint, codegen) use no clock or scheduler.
